transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess I'm just... having some trouble at work. If a breaker snaps, or, you know, someone drops a tool, I just... jump right out of my skin. Even if somebody just comes up behind me. And then my heart just keeps hammering. Long after everyone else has moved on and gone back to what they were doing, it just won't stop pounding. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried even when there's no immediate trigger or stressful event happening?
Not really. I don't... I don't just sit around worrying about nothing. So... no. Just what I said.
Do you ever feel a constant sense of anxiety or worry that seems to be there most of the time, even when nothing specific is happening?
I... I thought I just answered that. No. I don't just feel worried all the time. It's only when things happen, like I said.
Have you ever had sudden episodes where you feel intense fear or discomfort that comes on very quickly and reaches a peak within minutes, like a panic attack?
No. I don't... I don't get those. Like I said, it's just... when something loud happens. I don't just freak out for no reason.
Do you find yourself constantly on guard, even in safe situations, or watching out for possible threats even when there's no immediate danger?
No. I ain't looking over my shoulder all day. I just... do my work and go home. Like I keep saying, it's just the loud stuff. I don't walk around waiting for something bad to happen.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain places, situations, or activities because you're worried about being startled or hearing loud noises?

Yeah... I guess so. I mean, I make excuses at work. Try not to go near certain panels... or breakers. Some job sites, too. I just... I don't even like talking about that day. Because if I do, or if I'm around that stuff... once it starts in my head, I just can't shut it off. So I just stay away.
Do you ever get this same kind of reaction — like jumping or your heart pounding — in situations that aren't related to loud noises or work?
No. Just... just the loud stuff. Like I said.
Do you ever feel like you're reliving or re-experiencing a particular moment or event when you get startled?

Yeah... sometimes. Out of nowhere, I'll just... I'll see that flash in my head. Or hear the trainee yelling. Even if I'm just doing something normal, like loading tools in the truck. It just... it knocks me sideways. Like I'm right back there and it's happening again.
Do you often feel upset, angry, or guilty when you think about that moment or event that happened?
Yeah. I mean... I guess I'm just mad a lot. And... guilty. I just walk around feeling like that all the time. Like... like I failed that kid. And I just feel like everybody can see it on me.
Can you tell me more about that moment or event when you saw the flash and heard the trainee yelling — when did that happen, and what was going on?
It was... an arc-flash accident. On this retrofit job we were doing. It's been going on since then... about a year and a month now. I... I don't really want to get into all the details of it.
Since the accident, have you found yourself feeling detached from others or losing interest in things you used to care about?

Yeah, I guess. I just... I don't really do much anymore. I used to stay late at the shop, you know, fixing up cars... maybe play some ball or help the new guys figure things out. Now I just... I just go home and sit there. Phone rings, and I just let it ring. None of it really feels worth doing anymore.
Do you find yourself feeling angry or guilty most days since the accident, even when you're not thinking about it directly?

Yeah... I think I already said that. I just... I walk around mad and guilty all the time. Doesn't matter what I'm doing. It's just... always there. Like I failed that kid, and... and everybody can see it on me.
